descriptors.concept_name: Structure of Schedules to the Chartered Accountants Act
descriptors.definition: The First and Second Schedules of the Chartered Accountants Act define acts or omissions amounting to professional misconduct. They categorize violations into specific parts relating to members in practice, members in service, and members generally.
instrument_references: Section 22 of the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949
inclusion: Misconduct rules for members in practice
Misconduct rules for members in service
Misconduct rules for members generally
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between First Schedule provisions covering general or practice-specific rules and Second Schedule provisions handling severe professional misconduct categories.

descriptors.concept_name: Allowing Unqualified Persons to Practice in Accountant Name
descriptors.definition: A practicing chartered accountant commits professional misconduct by permitting any unqualified person to practice under their name. However, partners who are qualified chartered accountants in practice or firm employees may practice under that name.
instrument_references: Clause (1) of Part I of the First Schedule to the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949
inclusion: Permitting qualified partners to practice in the member's name
Permitting firm employees to practice in the member's name
exclusion: Allowing non-chartered accountants or relatives lacking qualifications to practice under the member's name
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between permitted use of a CA firm name by qualified internal partners or employees versus prohibited use by external unqualified individuals.

descriptors.definition: A practicing accountant must maintain client confidentiality and is guilty of professional misconduct if they disclose acquired professional information to third parties. Disclosure is permissible only with explicit client consent or when mandated by prevailing laws.
instrument_references: Clause (1) of Part I of the Second Schedule to the Chartered Accountants Act, 1949
inclusion: Disclosures explicitly authorized by the client
Disclosures mandatory under active legal frameworks
exclusion: Voluntary leaks of operational details post-assignment completion
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between mandatory or client-consented regulatory disclosures and unauthorized breaches of professional trust.

descriptors.concept_name: Council General Guidelines Maintenance of Books of Account
descriptors.definition: Practicing chartered accountants or their firms must maintain proper professional books of account including a cash book and a ledger. Failure to maintain these records constitutes professional misconduct regardless of thresholds in other tax statutes.
instrument_references: Clause (1) of Part-II of Second Schedule to The Chartered Accountants Act, 1949
inclusion: Maintaining a professional cash book
Maintaining a professional ledger
exclusion: Relying solely on income tax turnover exemptions to bypass professional account-keeping rules
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes ICAI professional accounting mandates from general tax law maintenance limits like Section 44AA of the Income Tax Act.

descriptors.definition: Members may publish informational write-ups about their firms and services provided they preserve the professional dignity and uphold truthfulness. These advertisements must avoid exaggerated claims, testimonials, client names, or prohibited formatting features.
inclusion: Honest and truthful service particulars
Mandatory display of membership number or FRN
Font size compliance up to limit
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes acceptable factual member write-ups from prohibited promotional marketing, client endorsements, and exaggerated claims.

descriptors.definition: Statutory auditors comprising ten or more members should refrain from conducting company branch audits, leaving them to smaller local firms. Exceptions apply if branch accounting records remain at the head office or significant operations occur at the branch.
inclusion: Branch audits handled by local firms with fewer than ten members
Statutory audit access rights preserved under company law
exclusion: Large statutory audit firms conducting branch audits where records are decentralized and operations are significant
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes recommendatory self-regulatory limits on large statutory audit firms handling branch audits from statutory statutory-access rights.

descriptors.concept_name: Relative Size Fee Disclosures for Entities
descriptors.definition: Practicing firms must disclose fee dependencies when gross annual professional fees from a single audit client exceed specific thresholds for consecutive years. Differentiated limits apply based on whether the entity is categorized as a public interest entity or a non-public interest entity.
inclusion: Fee disclosures exceeding forty percent for non-public interest entities over two consecutive years
Fee disclosures exceeding twenty percent for public interest entities over two consecutive years
exclusion: Firms with total fees not exceeding twenty lakh rupees
Government company and regulated public sector bank audits
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes fee dependency disclosure rules for public interest entities versus non-public interest entities.

descriptors.definition: Large companies are encouraged to associate practicing firms with fewer than five members as joint auditors. Senior firms should not object if a client requests the appointment of such a smaller firm.
inclusion: Associating smaller firms with less than five members as joint auditors
Client selection of joint auditors without senior firm obstruction
exclusion: Exclusive single-firm statutory audits for large enterprises without joint auditor collaboration
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes recommendations promoting small firm participation in joint audits from mandatory statutory appointment criteria.

descriptors.concept_name: Ratio Between Qualified and Unqualified Staff
descriptors.definition: Practicing audit firms should maintain a minimum staffing proportion of at least one qualified member for every five non-qualified staff members. This count excludes articled assistants, audit assistants, typists, and peons not directly engaged in professional audit work.
inclusion: Counting professional firm members directly engaged in audit work
Excluding administrative personnel like typists and peons from staff ratios
exclusion: Counting articled and audit trainees toward the non-qualified professional staff ratio computation
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes professional and non-qualified core audit staff from support staff and trainees for ratio compliance.

descriptors.concept_name: Disclosure of Interest by Auditors in Other Firms
descriptors.definition: Auditors should transparently disclose any payments received for rendering other services through alternate firms in which they hold a proprietary or partnership interest. This practice ensures transparency regarding ancillary service revenues collected via separate entities.
inclusion: Disclosing payments from secondary firms where the auditor is a partner
Disclosing payments from secondary entities where the auditor is a proprietor
exclusion: Concealing revenues generated through associated alternate service entities
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes primary statutory audit fee disclosures from transparent disclosures of payments received through distinct affiliated service firms.
